term.title: Pure Term Insurance
term.what: Pays the death benefit only. Zero maturity payout.
term.note: For every 1Cr of protection, pure term costs 6,000-18,000/year. This is the most cost-efficient life cover available. Invest the premium savings in mutual funds via SIP.

trop.title: Term + Return of Premium (TROP)
trop.what: Pays all premiums back if you survive the full policy term.
trop.note: You get your premiums back, but the effective return is only 2.5-4% XIRR — below inflation and below FD rates. Better than Endowment. Choose only if you cannot tolerate paying for pure term.

endowment.title: Endowment / Money Back Plan
endowment.what: A mix of life insurance + guaranteed savings.
endowment.maturity: Lower than premiums paid in real terms
endowment.note: You pay 6-8x more premium than term for the same cover. Returns are below Fixed Deposit rates. Classic trap: mixing insurance with investment destroys both. Use term + SIP instead.

ulip.title: ULIP (Market-Linked Plan)
ulip.what: Life insurance combined with a market-linked investment fund.
ulip.xirr: 7%-11% if equity performs; high charges in years 1-5
ulip.note: ULIPs can generate decent returns over 15+ years if equity performs. But high charges in years 1-5 significantly reduce real XIRR. Better alternative for most: pure term + separate ELSS SIP.

checklist.roomRentBody: Ensure the plan has NO sub-limit on room rent. A plan capping room rent at 5,000/day in a metro hospital means ALL linked charges (doctor fees, nursing, procedures) are also proportionally reduced. Avoid any plan with room rent sub-limits.
checklist.restorationBody: After one member uses up the sum insured, it should automatically restore — either once per year or unlimited. This is critical for families where multiple members may need hospitalisation. Ask: Does restoration apply to the same illness or a different illness? Unlimited is better.
checklist.ncbBody: Every claim-free year should increase your sum insured by 10-50% at no extra cost. Check: 1) What % NCB per year? 2) Is NCB protected after a small claim? 3) What is the maximum NCB cap? (50% is good, 100% is excellent)
checklist.pedBody: IRDAI 2025 rules: maximum PED waiting period is now 36 months (3 years) for new policies. Shorter is better. Look for plans with 36-month or less PED waiting. After the waiting period, your pre-existing conditions must be covered. Never hide a pre-existing condition — it is the #1 cause of claim rejection.
checklist.renewBody: Under IRDAI HIR 2016 Regulation 12, any policy renewed without a break cannot be denied renewal due to age. Ensure the policy explicitly states Lifelong Renewable. Never let your health policy lapse — you lose accumulated waiting period credits.
checklist.csrBody: CSR = claims settled / claims received x 100. Look for CSR above 95%. Verify from IRDAI's official annual report at irdai.gov.in — not from broker or comparison websites. Also check the Complaint Volume per 10,000 claims — lower complaints = smoother process.
checklist.tpaBody: Insurers that process claims in-house (no Third Party Administrator) typically settle faster and with fewer disputes. When buying, ask the insurer: Who processes my cashless claims at the hospital? In-house = better.
checklist.seniorBody: Adding parents 60+ to a family floater increases premium for the entire family. Consider a dedicated senior citizen plan. Compare: family floater vs separate senior plan pricing.
checklist.infantBody: Verify the insurer's newborn clause: Is the baby auto-covered from birth? Do you need to inform within 90 days? Is there an extra premium for adding the child?
checklist.floaterBody: Family floaters assume not all members claim in the same year. With 5+ members, the probability of multiple claims increases. Consider buying individual covers for high-risk members (seniors, those with pre-existing conditions) and keeping the floater only for younger, healthy members. Get quotes for both structures.
checklist.newbornCoverBody: Newborns should be covered from Day 1 or within 90 days without a fresh waiting period. Check the exact newborn clause in the policy wording document — not the brochure.
checklist.vaccineBody: Some plans cover routine vaccinations under OPD benefit. Check if this is included or available as an add-on. Useful for families with young children.
checklist.seniorCopayBody: Many plans add a co-payment clause for members above 60 — meaning you pay 10-20% of every claim. This defeats the purpose of insurance for seniors. Look specifically for plans with ZERO co-payment regardless of age.
checklist.seniorSeparateBody: Including parents above 60 in a family floater raises the entire family's premium significantly. Often it is cheaper to buy a dedicated senior citizen plan for parents and keep the main family floater for younger members. Get quotes both ways from IRDAI-registered insurers before deciding.
checklist.elderlyBody: Above age 70, very few insurers accept new proposals. If a parent has an existing policy, NEVER let it lapse — renewal cannot be denied under IRDAI rules. If no existing policy, check IRDAI's list of senior-friendly products at irdai.gov.in.
checklist.pedDeclareBody: Disclose ALL pre-existing conditions accurately in your proposal form. Under IRDAI's moratorium period rules (5 years as of 2024), after 5 years of continuous coverage, your insurer CANNOT reject claims citing non-disclosure (except proven fraud). Never hide conditions — claims get rejected at the worst time.
checklist.siWarnBody: In metro cities, a single surgery with ICU stay costs 3-8 lakhs on average. A cardiac bypass or cancer treatment can cost 8-20 lakhs. 5L cover is inadequate for metro hospitals. Consider 15-25L minimum for families in Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad.

irdaiRights.noAgeTitle: No Age Limit for New Policies
irdaiRights.noAgeBody: Insurers cannot deny new health insurance based on age. (IRDAI 2025 guideline)
irdaiRights.pedWaitBody: Waiting period for pre-existing diseases capped at 36 months for new policies. (IRDAI 2025)
irdaiRights.lifetimeBody: No policy can be denied renewal due to age if renewed without break. (IRDAI HIR 2016 Reg 12)
irdaiRights.moratoriumBody: After 5 years continuous coverage, insurer cannot reject claims citing non-disclosure (except fraud). (IRDAI Master Circular 2024)
irdaiRights.renewCapBody: Insurers cannot increase renewal premium for policyholders above 65 by more than 10% per year. (IRDAI Circular January 2025)
irdaiRights.freeLookBody: You can return the policy within 30 days for a full refund if unsatisfied. (IRDAI free-look rule)
irdaiRights.cashlessBody: Emergency cashless treatment allowed even at non-network hospitals. (IRDAI initiative 2024)
irdaiRights.gstBody: Individual health insurance premiums are GST exempt from September 22, 2025. (56th GST Council)
irdaiRights.portabilityBody: Switch insurer without losing accrued waiting period benefits. Apply 45 days before renewal.
irdaiRights.ombudsmanBody: Free dispute resolution if claim is rejected. File at irdai.gov.in — no lawyer needed.

howToBuy.step1Body: Before comparing premiums, decide your sum insured. Rule of thumb: 1 year of gross income OR minimum 10L for Tier 2/3, 15-25L for metro. Medical inflation is 14%/year in India — choose a sum insured that will still be adequate in 10 years.
howToBuy.step2Body: Go to irdai.gov.in → Statistics → Annual Report. Check Claim Settlement Ratio and Complaint Volume per 10,000 claims. Focus on insurers with CSR above 95% AND complaint ratio below 20.
howToBuy.step3Title: Read the Policy Wording — not the brochure
howToBuy.step3Body: The brochure shows benefits. The Policy Wording Document shows exclusions, sub-limits, and conditions. Search for: room rent, co-pay, sub-limit, waiting period, restoration. These are your risk areas.
howToBuy.step4Title: Get quotes for the same sum insured from 3 insurers
howToBuy.step4Body: Visit 3 insurer websites directly and get quotes for identical sum insured and members. Do not compare a 10L plan from one insurer with a 5L plan from another.
howToBuy.step5Title: Check network hospitals in your city
howToBuy.step5Body: Visit the insurer's website directly and search your preferred hospital name in their network. Do not rely on broker sites for this check — hospital lists change frequently.
howToBuy.step6Title: Buy directly from the insurer website
howToBuy.step6Body: Buying directly (insurer website or app) is cheaper than through a broker — no commission loading. You can still use a broker for advice, but buy direct to avoid markup.
howToBuy.step7Body: Fill the proposal form yourself. Disclose all pre-existing conditions, past surgeries, family medical history. Non-disclosure = claim rejection at the worst possible time.

compare.priorityGuide_csr: CSR = claims settled / claims received x 100. Look for CSR above 95%. Verify only at irdai.gov.in — Statistics — Annual Report. Third-party sites may show stale or adjusted numbers.
compare.priorityGuide_restoration: After one member exhausts cover, it should automatically restore — either once or unlimited per year. Unlimited restoration for different illnesses is the gold standard. Ask specifically whether restoration applies to the same illness too.
compare.priorityGuide_network: Before buying, search your preferred hospital on the insurer's own website. Hospital network lists change frequently — never rely on a broker or aggregator site for this verification.
compare.priorityGuide_opd: OPD benefit covers doctor consultations, diagnostics and medicines without hospitalisation. Check the annual OPD limit, sublimits per visit, and whether it requires a network doctor. Some plans offer OPD via teleconsultation.
compare.priorityGuide_wellness: Wellness rewards (gym, step count, health check-ups) reduce renewal premium in some plans. Read the fine print — reward redemption often requires specific apps or partner brands. Useful bonus, not a primary criterion.
compare.priorityGuide_claim_speed: Insurers with in-house claim processing settle cashless faster than TPA-based models. Ask the insurer directly: Who processes my cashless claims? Also check their median cashless settlement time.
compare.priorityGuide_senior: For members above 60, avoid plans with age-based co-payment (you pay 10-20% of every claim). Look for zero co-pay, higher room rent limits, and dedicated senior customer service. Consider a separate senior citizen plan.
compare.priorityGuide_child: For children under 5, verify the newborn clause (Day 1 or within 90 days). Check vaccination OPD benefit and whether paediatric sub-limits apply. Family floater sum insured should be adequate for a child hospitalisation.

cibil.title: CIBIL Score Guide
cibil.subtitle: Understand your score & loan impact
cibil.userEnteredDisclaimer: Score manually entered by you. FinCalix does not fetch or verify your score from TransUnion CIBIL or any credit bureau.
cibil.checkOnCibilWebsite: Check your official score on CIBIL website
cibil.exitModalBody: You are leaving FinCalix. We are not affiliated with TransUnion CIBIL or any credit bureau. Continue to cibil.com?
cibil.ratesIndicative: Indicative rates based on typical market ranges. Actual rates depend on lender policies, income & other factors. FinCalix is not a financial advisor or lender.
cibil.nhNote: RBI says banks cannot reject first-time borrowers solely for having no credit history
cibil.nhExplain: First-time borrower? RBI rules say banks cannot reject you for having no CIBIL. Your income and employment stability will be assessed.
cibil.vpDesc: Very high risk — multiple defaults or settlements
cibil.vpNote: Most banks will decline. Some NBFCs may offer at very high rates. Secured loans are better options.
cibil.poorDesc: High risk — missed payments or high utilisation
cibil.poorNote: Approval possible via NBFCs at higher rates. Banks may ask for co-applicant or collateral.
cibil.avgDesc: Moderate risk — some credit issues in history
cibil.avgNote: Approval possible but at higher rates. Larger down payment may be required.
cibil.goodNote: Most banks approve. Rates are reasonable. A 50-point improvement could save significantly.
cibil.vgNote: Standard market rates typically available. Lenders generally process applications faster for this score range. May be eligible for most loan products subject to lender underwriting.
cibil.exDesc: Very low risk — excellent credit discipline
cibil.exNote: Lowest market rates typically offered for this score range. Higher loan amounts and stronger negotiating position. Final approval still depends on lender's internal assessment.
cibil.improveSave: Improve from {{from}} to 780+ and save approximately {{amount}} in total interest
cibil.rbiSource: Source: RBI Master Direction on Credit Information, Jan 2025
cibil.approvalGreen: Lenders typically offer competitive rates for this score range. Final approval depends on lender's underwriting.
cibil.approvalYellow: NBFCs likely to approve, banks may be selective
cibil.approvalRed: Limited options — consider secured loans (gold, FD-backed)
cibil.tipPayTitle: Pay All EMIs & Bills On Time
cibil.tipPayDesc: Payment history = 35% of your score. Even ONE missed EMI can drop score by 50-100 points. Set auto-pay.
cibil.tipUtilDesc: If limit is ₹1L, never use more than ₹30,000. High utilisation signals financial stress.
cibil.tipOldDesc: Length of credit history = 15% of score. An old card improves your average account age.
cibil.tipAppDesc: Each application creates a hard inquiry. Space applications 6 months apart.
cibil.tipMixTitle: Maintain a Mix of Credit Types
cibil.tipMixDesc: Having both secured (home/car) and unsecured (credit card) credit = better score.
cibil.tipErrDesc: 1 in 5 reports has errors. Check free at cibil.com. Dispute errors — correction takes 30 days.
cibil.tipSecTitle: Get a Secured Credit Card (New Borrowers)
cibil.tipSecDesc: Start with a credit card against FD. Use for small purchases, pay full bill monthly. Score builds in 6 months.
cibil.howToImprove: How to Improve Your CIBIL Score
cibil.myth1: Checking my CIBIL score lowers it
cibil.fact1: Checking your OWN score is a soft inquiry — no impact. Only lender checks affect it.
cibil.myth2: Banks must accept me if I have 750+
cibil.fact2: CIBIL is one factor. Income, existing debts, employment also matter.
cibil.fact3: NH makes lenders nervous. Start building credit early with a secured card.
cibil.fact4: Closing old accounts REDUCES your average credit age — keep them open.
cibil.myth5: I can't get a loan with 650 score
cibil.fact5: NBFCs regularly lend at 600+. Gold loans need NO minimum score.
cibil.fact6: CIBIL updates monthly. Good behaviour for 6-12 months can improve 50-100 points.
cibil.ntcStep1: Get a Secured Credit Card against your FD (₹10,000 minimum). Use for small monthly expenses. Pay full bill.
cibil.ntcStep2: Take a small consumer loan. Even ₹5,000 EMI paid on time for 12 months builds a solid base.
cibil.ntcStep3: Maintain clean payment for 12 months. Your score will reach 700+ and qualify for most loans.
cibil.ntcStep4: Now apply for the loan you need — your clean short history is valued by lenders.
cibil.rbi1: RBI has NOT prescribed any minimum CIBIL score for loans
cibil.rbi2: Banks cannot reject first-time borrowers solely for having no credit history
cibil.rbi3: Each lender sets their own CIBIL policy based on board-approved risk framework
cibil.rbi4: CIBIL score is one factor — income, employment, existing debts also matter
cibil.rbi5: 4 RBI-approved credit bureaus: TransUnion CIBIL, Experian, Equifax, CRIF Highmark
cibil.rbi6: Free CIBIL check at cibil.com — once per year free. Checking your own score does NOT affect it
cibil.homeTip1: Score 760+ is ideal for home loans — most lenders use this as prime threshold
cibil.homeTip2: Every 50-point improvement can reduce home loan rate by 0.25-0.50%
cibil.homeTip3: On ₹40L for 20 years, 1% rate difference = ₹5-6L extra interest
cibil.personalTip1: Personal loan is unsecured — CIBIL score weighs most heavily here
cibil.personalTip2: Score below 650: avoid personal loans, consider secured alternatives
cibil.carTip1: Car is collateral — CIBIL less strict than personal loan
cibil.carTip2: EV car loans get 0.20% concession at some lenders
cibil.twTip1: EV two-wheeler loans are 0.5-1% lower than petrol for same CIBIL
cibil.eduTip1: Education loans assessed primarily on co-applicant (parent) CIBIL
cibil.goldTip1: Gold loans do NOT require minimum CIBIL — gold itself is collateral

tw.title: Two Wheeler Loan
tw.subtitle: Petrol, Electric & CNG — complete analysis
tw.rtoWaivedEv: Waived in many states for EVs
tw.ltvWarn: Most lenders cap at 90%. Verify with your lender.
tw.highBurden: High burden — consider lower tenure or higher down payment
tw.extraEmiTitle: What if you pay extra each month?
tw.rbiSource: Source: RBI Fair Practices Code, IRDAI guidelines
tw.rightAprDesc: Lender must disclose all charges, not just interest rate
tw.rightInsuranceDesc: You can choose your own insurance provider
tw.rightForeclosureDesc: You can close your loan anytime. Max charge ~4%
tw.rightPrepayDesc: You can make extra payments anytime
tw.rightFairCodeDesc: All lenders must follow RBI guidelines. Harassment is prohibited
tw.rightCreditDesc: On-time payments build your CIBIL. Late payments hurt it
tw.tipEvRateDesc: Electric two-wheeler loans are typically 0.5-1% cheaper than petrol due to green incentives. Ask your lender for EV-specific rates.
tw.tipCibilAlertDesc: With CIBIL below 700, expect rates of 15-22%. Pay all EMIs on time for 6 months to improve your score.
tw.tipDownPaymentDesc: A 10-15% down payment significantly reduces your EMI and total interest.
tw.tipTenureWarnDesc: 5-year tenure means you may pay more in interest than the bike's resale value. Consider 3 years.
tw.tipPremiumDesc: For bikes above ₹2L, banks offer better rates than NBFCs. Ensure CIBIL is 750+ for best rates.
tw.tipDocsDesc: Keep ready — Aadhaar, PAN, 3 months salary slips/ITR, 6-month bank statement, passport photo.
tw.tipHiddenDesc: Always ask for the total on-road price breakdown in writing. Check for hidden charges: extended warranty, accessories added without consent.
tw.evRunningCostDesc: Electric ₹0.15-0.30/km vs Petrol ₹2-3/km. At 8,000 km/year: Save ₹14,000-22,000/year.
tw.evBatteryDesc: Typical 4-6 year life. Replacement: ₹25,000-40,000. Factor into 5-year cost.
tw.evChargingDesc: Home charging is cheapest (₹5-8/unit). Full charge in 4-6 hours on standard socket.
tw.evResaleDesc: EV resale value is still uncertain vs petrol. Factor potential lower resale if selling in 3 years.
tw.petrolFixedRateDesc: Most two-wheeler loans are FIXED rate — EMI does not change. Confirm before signing.
tw.petrolForeclosureDesc: Charges are typically 2-4% on outstanding. Check before taking the loan.
tw.petrolInsBundleDesc: You have the RIGHT to buy insurance separately — often 30-40% cheaper from standalone insurers.
tw.petrolAccessoriesDesc: Adding ₹20,000 accessories at 14% for 3 years costs ₹24,800. Better to pay cash.

calcInfo.note: This calculator provides estimates for educational purposes only. Actual values may vary based on market conditions, institution policies, and individual circumstances.
calcInfo.defaultDesc: This financial calculator helps you make informed decisions by providing accurate estimates based on standard formulas and current market data.
calcInfo.emiDesc: The EMI Calculator helps you compute your Equated Monthly Instalment for any loan. Enter the loan amount, interest rate, and tenure to see your monthly payment, total interest, and full amortization schedule.
calcInfo.salaryHikeDesc: The Salary Hike Calculator helps you plan your next increment. Compare your hike against industry benchmarks, understand the tax impact, break down your CTC, and compare multiple job offers side by side.
calcInfo.sipDesc: The SIP Calculator shows how systematic monthly investments grow over time through the power of compounding. Enter your monthly amount, expected return rate, and investment period.
calcInfo.gstDesc: The GST Calculator helps you compute GST-inclusive or GST-exclusive prices. Quickly find the tax component for any amount at 5%, 12%, 18%, or 28% GST rates.
calcInfo.compoundInterestDesc: The Compound Interest Calculator shows how your money grows when interest is earned on both the principal and accumulated interest. Compare different compounding frequencies.
calcInfo.simpleInterestDesc: The Simple Interest Calculator computes interest earned on a principal amount at a fixed rate over a given period. Useful for understanding basic lending and deposit returns.
calcInfo.advancedSipDesc: The Advanced SIP Calculator includes step-up contributions, inflation adjustment, and detailed year-wise projections to help you plan long-term wealth creation more accurately.
calcInfo.cagrDesc: The CAGR Calculator computes the Compound Annual Growth Rate of an investment. Enter the initial value, final value, and period to find the annualised return.
calcInfo.homeLoanDesc: The Home Loan Calculator provides a complete analysis of your home loan including EMI, total interest, amortization schedule, and what-if scenarios for prepayment and rate changes.
calcInfo.personalLoanDesc: The Personal Loan Calculator helps you estimate your EMI and total cost for unsecured personal loans. Compare different tenures and rates to find the most affordable option.
calcInfo.carLoanDesc: The Car Loan Calculator computes your monthly EMI, total interest outgo, and provides a complete amortization schedule for your vehicle loan.
calcInfo.educationLoanDesc: The Education Loan Calculator helps students and parents estimate EMI and total repayment for education financing. Includes moratorium period and tax benefit analysis.
calcInfo.lumpsumDesc: The Lumpsum Calculator shows the future value of a one-time investment at a given rate of return over a specified period.
calcInfo.stepUpSipDesc: The Step-up SIP Calculator shows how increasing your SIP amount annually by a fixed percentage significantly boosts your long-term corpus through the power of compounding.
calcInfo.goalSipDesc: The Goal-based SIP Calculator works backwards from your target amount to tell you exactly how much you need to invest monthly to reach your financial goal.
calcInfo.mutualFundDesc: The Mutual Fund Returns Calculator helps you evaluate the performance of your mutual fund investments by computing actual returns including SIP and lumpsum modes.
calcInfo.swpDesc: The SWP Calculator helps retirees plan systematic withdrawals from their mutual fund corpus. See how long your money lasts at different withdrawal rates.
calcInfo.breakevenDesc: The Break-even Calculator determines how many units you need to sell to cover your fixed costs. Essential for business planning and pricing strategy.
calcInfo.fdDesc: The Fixed Deposit Calculator computes maturity value and interest earned on your FD. Compare quarterly vs monthly compounding and see year-wise growth.
calcInfo.rdDesc: The Recurring Deposit Calculator shows how your monthly deposits grow at a fixed interest rate over the deposit tenure with quarterly compounding.
calcInfo.ppfDesc: The PPF Calculator projects the maturity value of your Public Provident Fund over the 15-year lock-in period. PPF offers tax-free returns under Section 80C.
calcInfo.epfDesc: The EPF Calculator estimates your Employee Provident Fund corpus at retirement based on your basic salary, employer contribution, and expected interest rate.
calcInfo.npsDesc: The NPS Calculator projects your National Pension System corpus at retirement and estimates the monthly pension based on your contributions and asset allocation.
calcInfo.gratuityDesc: The Gratuity Calculator computes your gratuity payout based on years of service and last drawn salary. Gratuity is tax-free up to ₹20 lakh under current rules.
calcInfo.retirementDesc: The Retirement Calculator helps you determine how much you need to save monthly to build a corpus that sustains your desired lifestyle after retirement.
calcInfo.propertyYieldDesc: The Property Yield Calculator computes gross and net rental yield on your real estate investment. Compare yield against other investment options.
calcInfo.hraDesc: The HRA Calculator computes your House Rent Allowance exemption under Section 10(13A). Compare with the Section 80GG deduction for those without HRA.
calcInfo.incomeTaxDesc: The Income Tax Calculator computes your tax liability under both Old and New regimes for FY 2026-27. Compare regimes and find deductions to minimise your tax.
calcInfo.pomisDesc: The POMIS Calculator estimates monthly income from Post Office Monthly Income Scheme deposits. As a sovereign-backed scheme, POMIS offers fixed returns at the rate notified by Government of India (subject to quarterly revision).
calcInfo.scssDesc: The SCSS Calculator computes quarterly interest income from Senior Citizens Savings Scheme. SCSS offers one of the highest government-backed interest rates for senior citizens.
calcInfo.ssyDesc: The SSY Calculator projects the maturity value of Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana deposits. SSY offers tax-free returns and is designed for the girl child's education and marriage.
calcInfo.kvpDesc: The KVP Calculator shows when your Kisan Vikas Patra investment will double, based on the current Government-notified rate. As a sovereign-backed post office scheme, KVP offers fixed returns subject to quarterly rate revision by Government of India.
calcInfo.nscDesc: The NSC Calculator computes the maturity value of National Savings Certificate investments. NSC has a 5-year lock-in and qualifies for Section 80C deduction.
calcInfo.potdDesc: The POTD Calculator computes interest earned on Post Office Time Deposits across 1, 2, 3, and 5-year tenures. Government-backed with quarterly compounding.
